response: No, Kell alloimmunization in pregnancy is associated with fetal anemia, not thrombocytopenia. It can lead to hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN), but it does not typically cause thrombocytopenia. Alloimmunization to platelet antigens, such as PLA1 or HPA-1a, is more commonly associated with fetal thrombocytopenia.
